rows.whyNotBlockedSource: BOTH SOURCES BIND. This family was worth checking precisely because it looks blocked and is not: the census tier resolves JDF-683 and JDF-686 through the committed index, whose lexically first path for each is a d_source_packs path this container does not mount, so the row gate reports '2 of 2 source(s) do not bind'. Resolved by CONTENT across the mounted corpus, both are present and byte-exact in the Master Library: JDF-683 at 6b451ae32c01ef1e637a460df627d246e1b4a61d4ac4f166005a7349fa87202e and JDF-686 at abf997d8e701df0c74b1eb7833b35f30c006b50bf71b019abf7754d898433200. This is the wrongly-reported-BLOCKED_SOURCE pattern, and the source is not the problem here.

theActualBlocker.what: both forms are FLAT. JDF-683 (3 pages) and JDF-686 (2 pages) carry ZERO AcroForm fields and zero widgets between them.
theActualBlocker.consequence: official_pdf_fill on the AcroForm path has nothing to fill. Filling these two requires the measured flat-overlay renderer -- drawing text at coordinates measured against the printed rule lines -- which is a different renderStrategy (measured_flat_overlay), a different set of obligations, and a different class of visual risk: every value has to be proven not to land on printed ink, and there are no widget rectangles to measure against.
theActualBlocker.whyThatIsNotThisCohort: this cohort is the official-PDF-fill pattern and shares one AcroForm machinery. A flat-overlay family in the middle of it would be a different build sharing a lane name, and would need the flat-overlay verifier rather than the widget byte-proof this cohort's families are checked with.

rows.recommendation: MASTER_QUEUE records implementationStrategy official_pdf_fill for a family whose two forms have no fields. That classification is what should be corrected first; the family is buildable, by the flat-overlay lane, and its sources are in hand.
